Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Stratosphere Dynamics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, to ask a question during the Q&A session, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. A confirmation tone will indicate your line is in the queue. You may press star two if you're using a speakerphone. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Stratosphere Dynamics' Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Operating Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Strategy Officer; David Brooks, Chief Marketing Officer; and Thomas Grant, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning. Stratosphere Dynamics delivered a solid performance in Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering value to our shareholders. Today, I will cover several key areas starting with the defense budget outlook and its impact on our company.

As we enter this period, we're uniquely positioned at the intersection of next-generation air dominance, hypersonic strike, and integrated air-and-missile defense systems, with a $28.7 billion funded backlog at the start of the year—up 12% year-over-year—and multi-year awards across our F-47 Lightning II sustainment, Vanguard Hypersonic Glide Vehicle, and Sentinel Space-Based Interceptor programs. Globally, defense spending is experiencing a structural upswing, projected to hit $2.4 trillion in calendar 2024 according to SIPRI estimates, marking a 6.8% real-terms increase from 2023, propelled by escalating great-power competition and regional flashpoints. In the U.S., the FY2025 President's Budget Request proposes a topline DoD discretionary outlay of $849.8 billion—essentially flat nominally against FY2024's $886 billion NDAA authorization, but showing real growth adjusted for 2.5% inflation. The focus is on procurement at $167 billion, down 5% year-over-year due to prior F-35 Economic Order Quantity buys, offset by a strong $145 billion in RDT&E, up 2%, emphasizing hypersonics, collaborative combat aircraft, and resilient space architectures.

Congress remains supportive, with House and Senate Armed Services Committees indicating plans to increase the topline by $20-30 billion through NDAA reconciliation, prioritizing Pacific deterrence. Tailwinds include the FY2024 supplemental's $61 billion Ukraine aid, with $23 billion to U.S. industry for 155mm artillery and ATACMS restock, and a proposed $95 billion FY2025 supplemental for Israel, Taiwan, and Ukraine, potentially adding $15-20 billion in missile and munitions production. In Europe, NATO allies are pushing toward the 2% GDP target, with collective spending at €380 billion in 2024—up 18% year-over-year. Poland's 4.1% GDP commitment means $40 billion in new buys, including our Patriot PAC-3 MSE systems and F-47 integrations. Germany's €100 billion Sondervermögen is committed through 2027, funding 35 additional F-47s and Eurofighter Typhoon upgrades with our AESA radar enhancements. In Asia-Pacific, Japan's record ¥8.7 trillion ($55 billion) FY2025 budget—7.5% growth—includes $4 billion for GCAP tech maturation, where our digital twin and AI/ML simulation tech sets us up for JAGUAR engine co-development. Australia's AUKUS pillar-two ramps to AUD 368 billion over 30 years, offering hypersonic and SSN sustainment. Middle East markets like Saudi Arabia rebound with Vision 2030's $75 billion for localization, including our THAAD co-production in Riyadh achieving 15% localization on Phase III interceptors.

For Stratosphere Dynamics, our defense segment—85% of FY2024 revenue—grew 11% organically to $6.2 billion in Q3, driven by a 22% backlog conversion on high-margin sustainment. We guide 9-11% revenue growth in FY2025 for this segment, with EPS accretion of $2.15-2.35 per share. In air dominance, the F-47 Lot 16 award of 48 aircraft at $4.2 billion—EOQ pricing at $105 million per unit, down 8% from Lot 14—sets us for FRP in 2026. NGAD risk-reduction funding of $2.5 billion aligns with our CCA demonstrator, backed by $450 million in IR&D for autonomy stacks targeting 40% cost savings via attritable swarms. In hypersonics and missiles, Vanguard HGV PoR unlocks $8.9 billion over five years; Q3 brought $1.2 billion in restock post-Ukraine/Red Sea. Our Dark Eagle hit Mach 20, de-risking $3.7 billion Army pipeline, with margins to 14.5% in FY2025 from titanium forging localization. For missile defense and space, Sentinel Phase 2's $1.1 billion supports Kill Vehicle tech at 95% intercept probability; space backlog up 18% to $4.1 billion, with Vulcan Centaur favored for NSSL Phase 3 Lane 2 at 15% lower lifecycle costs.

Strategically, we're advancing on program stability—92% of PoRs funded through FY2026—international diversification with FMS/direct sales at 28% of backlog (up from 22%, 15% CAGR to 2028), and tech inflection via $720 million FY2025 IR&D (12% of sales) for digital engineering cutting F-47 cycles by 30% and 300kW laser for USN HELIOS. Risks like CRs deferring $5-7 billion are buffered by $12 billion unfunded backlog; supply chain inflation at 4-5% for composites mitigated by Japanese dual-sourcing. This validates our 10-year 8-10% CAGR, ROIC to 18% by FY2027.

Next, our expansion of service offerings and customer base. We've pivoted toward a high-margin, recurring revenue services model while broadening our market, positioning us to grab more of the $1.2 trillion global A&D aftermarket through 2030 per Deloitte. Services—MRO, sustainment, logistics—surged 32% year-over-year to $1.8 billion in Q3, now 42% of top line with 24.5% EBITDA margins, up 450 basis points. Key initiatives: our AeroPredict AI for predictive maintenance and digital twins on 1,200+ F-35 airframes, cutting downtime 28% and securing $450 million PBL contracts using IoT and 15 petabytes of data, extending to hypersonics. Advanced manufacturing with DED and laser powder bed fusion ramped titanium parts for B-21, slashing lead times 40%, waste 35%, unlocking $320 million from Northrop. Space domain awareness services via C4ISR heritage won $150 million with Space Force's PWSA, tapping $18 billion market.

Customer expansion: new bookings $4.2 billion, 55% up, book-to-bill 1.4x. U.S.: $900 million MQ-9 MRO for Army. Europe: backlog up 68% to $2.1 billion, £450 million PBL for Tempest, Rheinmetall Eurofighter. Asia-Pacific: 45% growth to $750 million, $1.2 billion AUKUS F-35A. Middle East: $600 million UAE F-16, Saudi MoUs. Commercial: 22% to $300 million Airbus A350 nacelles; space $200 million SpaceX/Blue Origin. Anchored in $250 million CapEx, $1.4 billion Vector Aerospace M&A, Palantir alliances; 85% recurring shields from FY2025 caps. Guide 25-30% growth FY2025, 50% of revenue by 2027.

Moving to performance of our priority defense programs. These drive most growth, underpinning $52 billion backlog, fueled by FY24 NDAA and international awards from Europe/Indo-Pacific tensions. NGAD/PCA: Q3 sales $1.8 billion, up 22% YoY, LRIP Lot 3 deliveries at 98% on-time, margins 14.2% via MBSE/digital twins cutting labor 18%; OMS 2.0 for CCA, EAC green on $16 billion EMD, $450 million international. Hypersonics HAWC-2/CPS: $1.2 billion, 35% up, 2.1x book-to-bill to $14 billion backlog; GPX-2 Mach 12+ at 95% TPS yield; margins 12.8% despite inflation, $600 million UK AUKUS, $300 million South Korea. IAMD/NGI/PAC-3: $950 million, 18% up, 150 MSE early, 92% kill chain, 13.5% margins via GaN AM; Middle East 40% QoQ, $11 billion backlog. Unmanned MQ-Next/CCA: $750 million, 28% up, IOC Group 5, 1,200 Red Flag hours 85% autonomy; $400 million NATO/Poland. Aggregate $5.2 billion sales, 75% revenue, 13.4% margins +220 bps, backlog +15%; $500 million supply chain resilience, 2.2x book-to-bill affirms 20-22% FY24 growth.

Then, geopolitical factors affecting defense spending. SIPRI shows $2.44 trillion global in 2023, 6.8% up—the biggest since Cold War—with 5-7% CAGR to 2028. U.S. FY24 NDAA $886 billion, 3.2% real growth, procurement/RDT&E +8/10%, adding $1.8 billion F-35 Lots 17-19. Europe: Ukraine $100 billion aid, $44 billion U.S. PDA; FMS +150% to $2.1 billion, Poland $12 billion, Germany €100 billion; backlog +45% to $9.2 billion. Indo-Pacific 9% up: AUKUS $368 billion, Japan $320 billion LRASM, Taiwan $19 billion; 18% Q2 sales. Middle East: Houthi/Iran threats, $14.5 billion Israel aid, Saudi $60 billion THAAD/F-15EX; GCC PAC-3 +120%, $4.8 billion backlog. 25% RDT&E on hypersonics/DEW/C4ISR, domestic rare earths, 95% skills fill. FY24 guide up: $18.5-19.0 billion revenue +12%, EPS $14.80-15.20, backlog >$30 billion.

Our strategic priorities and outlook for next quarter/year. With EPS $2.85 beating by 12 cents, $48 billion backlog +15%, 1.2x book-to-bill. Priority 1: production ramp/supply chain—180 F-35s, resolve titanium/composites via Spirit/Hexcel, +10% to 200 in '25; PAC-3 $2.1 billion, $250 million Tucson capex for 30% hypersonics/JASSM. Priority 2: tech/digital—NGSS $1.8 billion MDA sats Vulcan Q2 '25; MQ-Next 95% trials, $450 million AI/ML; 10% SAF, hybrid AAM. Priority 3: international—Europe $3.2 billion F-35/Patriot GCAP; Asia SM-3 Japan/Australia; Middle East $1.5 billion THAAD; UAE/Poland localization. Q4 revenue $2.6-2.7 billion +9%, EPS $2.95-3.05; FY24 $10.8-11.0 billion, EPS $11.40-11.60, FCF $1.2 billion. FY25 8-10% to $11.7-12.1 billion, EPS +12-15%, margins >14%, 1.15x book-to-bill $52 billion. Risks: labor/cyber/CRs, inflation to 3-4%.

Free cash flow generation and utilization. FCF $1.4 billion Q3 +28% YoY, 9 months $4.2 billion toward $6.0-6.5 billion FY. Ops cash $2.1 billion +22%: Aeronautics $450 million DSO 52 days F-35/FMS; Missiles $620 million PAC-3/JASSM 4.2x turns, localization; Space $380 million GPS IIIF digital twins. EBITDA 15.8% +150 bps $145 billion backlog 40% int'l. Capex $700 million: 45% hypersonic Huntsville, 30% F-35 FRAP, 25% AI ERP. U.S. 65%, Europe 18%, Asia 10%, ME 7%. Utilization: $850 million returns—$450 million div $1.35/share +22nd increase, $400 million buyback 1.2 million shares; $350 million debt to 1.8x, pension $50 million. Reinvest $200 million: $120 million DEW, $50 million AM C-130J, $30 million blockchain. Q4 $1.8-2.2 billion.

Drivers of aftermarket performance. $1.25 billion +18% Q2, 42% top line, EBITDA 29.2% +210 bps. Fleet utilization: commercial 87% pre-pandemic, narrowbody 11.2 hrs/day; F-35 +14% hours, +25% parts. Maintenance cycles: 1,420 visits +16%, A320neo 28 days; defense PBL 92% availability, structural repairs 8,000+ hours. North America 55% +20% KC-46; EMEA 25% Ryanair/UK F-35; Asia 28% IndiGo LEAP. DES AI/digital twins -22% downtime $85 million parts; drone hybrids $200 million. Q3 $1.3-1.35 billion, FY 17-19%; $150 million academy.

Finally, backlog growth. Total $128.5 billion, +$8.2 billion (6.8% q/q, 17.2% y/y) from $120.3/$109.7 billion—8th straight quarter. Defense $92.4 billion +$6.9 billion (8.1% q/q, 22.4% y/y): F-47 Lots 18/19 $4.1 billion, Poland $1.2 billion FMS $2.3 billion 1.25x 78% funded. Missiles $18.7 billion +$1.0 billion GPI $650 million Pacific $400 million. Space $10.2 billion +$300 million Orion Artemis $450 million. Commercial $7.2 billion flat +5% y/y TitanJet $800 million. North America 62% $79.7 billion NDAA; Europe +28% $22.1 billion AUKUS; Asia +19% $15.4 billion; ME $4.3 billion. $1.2 billion digital/AI, EPA clauses; FY24 >$135 billion 1.2x, 25-30% conversion $32-34 billion revenue.

We are particularly excited about the recent advancements in our F-47 Lightning II program and its potential to drive significant revenue growth in the coming years. We are seeing strong demand for our defense systems, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily.

Michael Rivera:
Thank you, Johnathan. Now, let's turn to the financials. In Q3, we reported revenue of $7.4 billion, representing an 11% increase year-over-year. Our earnings per share were $2.85. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $4.8 billion in cash and equivalents. Our guidance for the full year remains unchanged at the midpoint. We are actively managing our costs and investing in key growth initiatives. We are also focused on returning capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Our specific financial highlights include gross margin of 22.8%, operating income of $1.45 billion, and free cash flow of $1.4 billion.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Michael. Operationally, we have seen significant improvements in our supply chain management, allowing us to increase production rates on key programs like the F-47 Lightning II and hypersonic systems. We are also investing in automation and digital technologies to improve efficiency and reduce costs. Specifically, we've localized titanium forging and composites sourcing, cutting lead times by 25% and enhancing resilience against global disruptions.

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thank you, Elena. On the technology front, we're making significant strides in our next-generation propulsion systems for hypersonics and air dominance platforms. We anticipate these advancements will give us a competitive edge in the years to come. More specifically, our Dark Eagle and HAWC derivatives have achieved Mach 20+ with advanced CMC transpiration cooling, de-risking multi-billion pipelines while expanding margins through supply chain efficiencies.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. From a strategic perspective, we are actively evaluating potential acquisitions that would complement our existing portfolio and expand our market reach, particularly in rotorcraft MRO and space sustainment. We are also focused on developing new business models that will allow us to capture emerging opportunities. For instance, alliances like Palantir for AI supply chain and co-development in GCAP position us for sixth-gen tech transfer and AUKUS Pillar II.

David Brooks:
Thank you, Lisa. From a marketing perspective, we are seeing great success with our new branding campaign emphasizing lifecycle partnership in contested environments, which is resonating well with DoD primes and international allies. We are also leveraging digital channels to reach new customers and increase brand awareness. The results are a 55% increase in new bookings and book-to-bill above 1.4x across regions.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. As a reminder, to ask a question, press star then one. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the backlog growth and its implications for FY25 visibility?

Johnathan Hale:
Certainly, Emily. Our record $128.5 billion backlog, up 17.2% year-over-year, provides exceptional multi-year visibility, with strong conversion pacing 25-30% drawdown to support $32-34 billion revenue this year. Defense leads at 8.1% sequential growth, funded at 78%, insulating against CRs while international exposure diversifies risks.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
Hi, thanks. I'm curious about the drivers of aftermarket performance amid fleet utilization trends?

Michael Rivera:
David, aftermarket strength at 18% growth to $1.25 billion stems from 12% blended utilization uptick—commercial to 87% recovery, F-35 hours +14%—and normalizing maintenance cycles with 1,420 visits, aided by DES AI cutting downtime 22%. This annuity-like segment bolsters margins to 29.2%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Rachel Lee:
Regarding the performance of priority defense programs like NGAD and hypersonics?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Rachel, priority programs generated $5.2 billion or 75% of Q3 revenue, up 24%, with NGAD at 14.2% margins via MBSE and hypersonics 2.1x book-to-bill on Mach 12+ milestones. Backlog diversified 45% international supports 20-22% FY24 growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Thompson with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Alex Thompson:
Question about geopolitical factors and their sustainment into FY25?

Lisa Chen:
Alex, geopolitics like Ukraine, Indo-Pacific tensions, and Middle East conflicts drive structural 5-7% global spending CAGR, with U.S. supplementals and NATO 2%+ pledges fueling $4.2 billion Q3 bookings. Our portfolio—F-35, PAC-3, hypersonics—is aligned for continued tailwinds.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
